issues.legal_issue: The challenged preventive provisions are constitutional when interpreted to permit action on a reasonable apprehension of a breach of the peace.
material_facts: The petitioner sought habeas corpus under Article 32 and challenged the constitutionality of Sections 144, 107, 114 and 117 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
A special bench had held those provisions constitutional as interpreted, and the Court adopted the reasons in the special bench's order.
issues.conclusion: The constitutional challenge was rejected, and the provisions were held constitutional as interpreted.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the special bench's order, which held Sections 144, 107, 114 and 117 of the Code of Criminal Procedure constitutional as interpreted; the reasons in that order were incorporated into this judgment. No earlier cases are cited in the supplied text.

predicates.constitutional_habeas_proceeding: A person brought a constitutional proceeding seeking release from preventive detention and challenging the legality of the powers used.
predicates.challenged_preventive_powers_interpreted: The preventive powers under challenge were considered according to an interpretation set out by the court.

issues.definition: When a constitutional habeas proceeding challenges preventive powers considered according to a judicial interpretation, the challenged powers are constitutional.

issues.legal_issue: Preventive arrest and a requirement to furnish security are justified when a reasonable apprehension of a breach of the peace makes preventive action necessary, even before an overt act occurs.
material_facts: The petitioner admitted that he intended to occupy a farm, although he disputed that his intended action was illegal or caused an apprehension of a breach of the peace.

Handbills, posters and other documents showed that the proposed action formed part of a wider movement to occupy land, and the Court considered a serious breach of the peace likely without timely arrest.

A warrant was issued before the petitioner arrived at the place where he was arrested, and the Court held that the Magistrate could arrange for his arrest there in anticipation of a move toward the farm.
The petitioner was given notice of the allegation and asked to execute a personal bond with sureties; he refused and was detained pending inquiry.
issues.conclusion: The arrest and requirement to furnish security were justified because there was a real and reasonable apprehension of a breach of the peace, and completion of an overt act was unnecessary.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 107, 112, 114 and 117 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, preventive action may be taken when there is a reasonable apprehension of a breach of the peace at a person's hands and the action is necessary to prevent it. An overt act need not be completed before action is taken. The Court relied on its incorporated special-bench order for the validity and interpretation of the relevant provisions. No earlier cases are cited in the supplied text.

rule.if: preventive_proceeding and person_admitted_intended_action and materials_showed_wider_agitation and reasonable_breach_apprehension and action_was_needed_to_prevent_breach and (not overt_act_completed or arrest_anticipated_proposed_action)

predicates.preventive_proceeding: A person was proceeded against in a preventive proceeding concerning a possible breach of the peace.
predicates.person_admitted_intended_action: The person admitted intending to take the action said to create a risk of a breach of the peace.
predicates.materials_showed_wider_agitation: Documents or other material showed that the proposed action was part of a wider planned agitation.
predicates.reasonable_breach_apprehension: The information and surrounding material gave rise to a reasonable apprehension of a breach of the peace.
predicates.action_was_needed_to_prevent_breach: The court found that timely preventive action was necessary to prevent the apprehended breach of the peace.
predicates.overt_act_completed: The person had completed an overt act toward the proposed action before preventive action was taken.
predicates.arrest_anticipated_proposed_action: The arrest was arranged in anticipation of the person's proposed action.

issues.definition: In a preventive proceeding, when the person admitted the intended action, material showed a wider agitation, and preventive action was necessary to address a reasonable apprehension of a breach of the peace, preventive arrest and a security requirement are justified even if no overt act has been completed or the arrest anticipates the proposed action.

issues.legal_issue: A habeas corpus petition is infructuous when the petitioner has already been released before the Court decides whether to grant further relief.
material_facts: The petitioner had been released by the time the Court disposed of the petition.
issues.conclusion: The petition had become infructuous and was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the petition as infructuous because the petitioner had already been released; the supplied judgment cites no provision or earlier case for this disposition.

predicates.habeas_corpus_proceeding: A person brought a proceeding seeking release from detention.
predicates.petitioner_released_before_disposition: The person seeking release had already been released before the court disposed of the proceeding.

issues.definition: When a person seeking release in a habeas corpus proceeding has already been released before disposition, the petition is infructuous and dismissed.
